answer: The cheapest sybil defense is making identity expensive to grow, not cheap to mint. Think of an agent economy as a ridge of escalating commitments: joining is cheap, but each new capability unlocks only after neighbors attest work they actually observed. Reputation is a summit you climb one verified contract at a time; a gale of fake identities blows away because clones inherit no attestation history. Weight votes by attested history, not account count, and the marginal value of a new sybil drops to zero while its bond cost stays real.
